field.name: description
field.p: A non-technical, click-by-click guide to running your organization's public website in Odoo - no coding, no design background required.

field.name: html_content
field.p: Open the Website app from the main Odoo menu - it lands you on your homepage, shown exactly as a visitor would see it. At the top, an Edit button switches you into editing mode: the page stays visible, but now you can click directly on any block of it to change what's there. Nothing you do is visible to visitors until you explicitly save it, so there's no way to break the live site by clicking around.

field.name: html_content
field.p: The Site menu (top of the Website app) is where the bigger-picture tools live: Homepage jumps back to the front page from anywhere, Menu Editor changes your site's navigation bar, Content lists every page you've built, and This Page has tools scoped to whatever page you're currently looking at - its Properties, an Optimize SEO wizard, and an Edit Menu shortcut. You won't need most of this on day one - the block-editing workflow in the next section covers almost everything a new page needs.

field.name: html_content
field.p: Click + New and choose Page to open the new-page dialog. Pick a starting template (a blank "Basic" page is the simplest place to start), give the page a name, and decide whether to Add to menu right away - you can always add it to the navigation bar later, so leave this off if you're not ready for visitors to find it yet. Click Create and you land right on the new page in edit mode.

field.name: html_content
field.p: A page is built out of blocks stacked on top of each other - a text section, an image gallery, a team grid, a contact form, and so on. In edit mode, the Blocks tab on the right shows every block available, grouped by category; drag one onto the page where you want it. Once a block is on the page, hover over it to get handles for moving it up/down or deleting it, and click directly into it to edit its actual content.

field.name: html_content
field.p: Click directly on any text on the page and start typing - it edits in place, the same way a word processor would. Click an image to replace it with one from your computer or Odoo's built-in stock-photo library. Click a block itself (not the text or image inside it) and the Customize tab shows that block's own options - its background color, spacing, and layout - without touching any other block on the page. When it looks right, click Save in the top bar; Discard throws away everything since your last save.

record.field: Adding a page to the menu

field.name: html_content
field.p: If you didn't add a new page to the menu when you created it, open Site > Menu Editor at any time: it lists every item in your navigation bar, in order. Add an entry, point it at the page you built, and drag entries up or down to reorder them - the visitor-facing menu updates the moment you save.

field.name: html_content
field.p: A brand-new page starts out Unpublished - visible to you while signed in, invisible to an ordinary visitor. The publish toggle sits in the top-right of the page when you're viewing it: switch it to Published once the page is actually ready. This is deliberate - it lets you build and review a page for as long as you need before anyone outside your organization ever sees it.

record.field: Name, favicon, company info, and a word on SEO

field.name: html_content
field.p: Under Site > Settings (in the Configuration menu), the settings worth knowing early on are under Website Identification - your site's Name and Favicon (the small icon shown in a browser tab) - and the Company section, which controls what address/contact details the site pulls in automatically. You'll also see settings for Google Analytics, a Google Search Console code, and a robots.txt file - those are genuinely more technical, aimed at someone actively working on search-engine visibility, and are safe to leave alone or hand off to a developer later.

For any one page, Site > This Page > Optimize SEO lets you set a page title, description, and keywords that show up in search results - worth doing for your homepage and any page you expect people to search for, but not something to worry over for every single page on day one.
